newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila shares end lower, in consolidation mode.
newsitem.headline: Manila shares end lower, in consolidation mode.

text.p: * Focus seen shifting to speculative issues
Manila shares closed down in listless trade on Wednesday for the third consecutive day, remaining firmly in consolidation mode, traders said.
"The market is weak and still consolidating. The index will likely stay above 2,900 points in the near term," said Ramon Borja, analyst at Dharmala Securities (Phils) Inc.
The main index slipped 23.53 points, or 0.77 percent, to 3,049.59 points, off its intra-day low of 3,045.84.
"It's a healthy correction because volume is thin at 1.7 billion. It looks like a time to accumulate stocks," said Teresa Lee, Lippo Securities assistant vice-president.

Focus shifted to tertiary issues as gainers included gaming firm Greater Asia Resources Corp and hotel-casino operator Waterfront Philippines Inc. Selling was seen in blue chips such as Petron Corp and San Miguel Corp.
"People prefer to be liquid now and are positioning themselves, waiting for a market trend to emerge," said Jonas Ferrer, research head at Pryce Securities Inc.
